newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton down on low demand, new arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton down on low demand, new arrivals.

text.p: Cotton prices extended losses on the local market on Wednesday, dealers said.
"Mill demand was low while rising new crop arrivals dragged prices downward," one dealer said.

Daily crop arrivals in Punjab rose to 24/25 thousand bales (170 kg each) against a daily average of 15/18 thousand bales last week. In spot deals Bengal-deshi fell to 870/890 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) from 885/925 rupees. Punjab saw-ginned slid to 1,570/1,725 rupees per maund. Gujarat Sankar-4 fell to 20,000/20,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) from 20,500/20,800 rupees. -- Bombay Newsroom +91-22-265 9000
